title: Best Rice Cookers UK
short: Eight rice cookers compared on the rice they actually produced, from a £25 microwave pot to fuzzy-logic and induction models and an Instant Pot.
intro: A rice cooker's real test is whether it gives consistently fluffy rice without watching the pan. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where each cooker was timed on two scoops of long-grain and short-grain white rice (excluding the recommended five-minute rest), then used across its other functions. Expert Reviews updated the guide in May 2025 and prices are as reviewed. Where the source states no drawback for a model, this guide says so rather than inventing one.

products.name: Rice Cooker and Steamer 19750
products.best_for: Family dinners, entertaining or weekend batch cooking on a small budget
products.key_spec: Up to ten cups of rice, auto switch-off, keep-warm, steamer basket, non-stick removable bowl
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a neat, crowd-pleasing cooker that's really helpful for big family dinners, with fuss-free controls, auto switch-off after cooking and a keep-warm function. It doubles as a steamer using a basket for fish, potatoes and vegetables with no added fat, and comes with a spatula and measuring cup, in a stainless steel finish smart enough to leave on display.
pros: Makes up to ten cups of rice
Doubles as a steamer
Auto switch-off and keep-warm function
Smart stainless-steel finish and glass lid
cons: Expert Reviews noted no specific drawbacks
products.search: Russell Hobbs Rice Cooker and Steamer 19750

products.name: Bamboo Induction Rice Cooker
products.best_for: Keen cooks who want a connoisseur's fuzzy-logic induction cooker with many presets
products.key_spec: Fuzzy-logic chip with induction heating, touchscreen with ten presets including GABA and Tahdig crust, steam, bake, slow cook
products.summary: Expert Reviews loved this high-tech eight-person cooker, which adjusts temperature during cooking and offers presets for white, brown and short-grain rice plus a Yumami setting for sweeter rice, a porridge or congee mode and a crust setting for Persian Tahdig. The GABA setting gave a noticeably softer, slightly different-tasting brown rice, though testers couldn't confirm the extra nutrients claimed, and it also steams, bakes cakes and slow cooks.
pros: Fuzzy logic and induction give smart temperature adjustment
Wide range of presets including brown rice, congee and Tahdig
Multi-functional: steams, bakes and slow cooks
Alerts at ten minutes left and keeps warm afterwards
cons: The GABA setting's claimed nutrient benefit couldn't be confirmed in testing
products.search: Yum Asia Bamboo induction rice cooker

products.name: Mini Rice Cooker
products.best_for: One or two-person households wanting a fuzzy-logic cooker in a small footprint
products.key_spec: 0.6L capacity, 22.5 x 30 x 21cm, Fuzzy Logic microprocessor, also steams and makes yoghurt, porridge and cakes
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a straightforwardly great compact choice with one of the cheaper Fuzzy Logic chips you'll find, which produced excellent, replicable results on long-grain, basmati and brown rice. It cooked a couple of minutes faster than other models tested and can steam rice and dim sum at the same time, handle vegetables and grains together and make yoghurt, porridge and cakes.
pros: Compact but a solid 0.6L capacity
Fuzzy Logic gives consistent results on long-grain, basmati and brown rice
A couple of minutes faster than other models tested
Versatile: steams, makes yoghurt, porridge and cakes
cons: Not the lowest-priced small rice cooker
products.search: Yum Asia Panda Mini rice cooker

products.name: 45002 M-Cuisine Microwave Rice Cooker
products.best_for: Occasional rice cooks in flats, house shares or student accommodation
products.key_spec: Microwavable pot with lid, included cup measure, dishwasher-safe, 2L
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this the easiest way to fluffy white rice for those who cook rice occasionally: measure rice and water with the included cup, put the lid on and microwave, with no watching over a saucepan. It's stylish, dishwasher-safe and small enough for tiny kitchens, at a great price.
pros: Easy fluffy white rice with no pan-watching
Dishwasher-safe and small for tiny kitchens
Great price, includes a cup measure
cons: Best suited to occasional rice cooking rather than regular use
products.search: Joseph Joseph M-Cuisine microwave rice cooker

products.name: Mini Multi Cooker
products.best_for: Small or shared kitchens wanting a budget multi-cooker that still feeds a family
products.key_spec: 1.4L, white, brown and quick-cook rice modes, also slow cooks and makes yoghurt, porridge and cakes
products.summary: Expert Reviews found surprisingly good rice for the price, with little difference in taste or texture compared with pricier cookers, and an easy-to-use interface that more than makes up for its clunky looks. Some steam escaped from under the lid unlike on pricier models, but this didn't harm the rice if left to sit after fluffing, and despite the mini label it can feed up to four people.
pros: Surprisingly good performance for the price
Easy-to-use interface
Feeds up to four people
Slow cooks and makes yoghurt, porridge and cakes
cons: Some steam escapes from under the lid

products.name: Duo Evo Plus
products.best_for: Buyers who want a rice cooker and a pressure cooker in one appliance
products.key_spec: 5.7L, 10 functions, rice presets, pressure, saute, steam, slow cook, yoghurt, sous vide
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the pressure cooking function worked like a dream on even the toughest cuts, and the rice presets produced fluffy white grains for three people in around 22 minutes. It saves owning separate appliances, with a stylish, easy-to-use digital interface that suits first-time pressure cooker users.
pros: Pressure cooking breaks down even tough cuts
Rice presets gave fluffy white rice in about 22 minutes
Saute, steam, slow cook and more in the same pot
Stylish, easy-to-use digital interface
cons: Expert Reviews noted no specific drawbacks

products.name: Risotto Plus
products.best_for: Buyers with a moderate budget who mainly cook long-grain rice and risotto
products.key_spec: Multipurpose rice and risotto cooker with a well-designed steamer
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this not the flawless five-star appliance expected from Sage, but reasonably inexpensive, good looking and easy to use, with a handy steamer for cooking vegetables alongside rice. It cooks long-grain rice to a good standard in very little time, though you have to jump through hoops to get good short-grain rice, the mess it makes needs extra cleanup, and it doesn't reach the standard of pricier cookers.
pros: Reasonably inexpensive and good looking
Easy to use, with a well-designed steamer
Long-grain rice cooked to a good standard quickly
cons: Hoops to jump through to master quality short-grain rice
The mess it generates needs extra cleanup
Not up to the standard of more expensive rice cookers
products.search: Sage by Heston Blumenthal Risotto Plus

products.name: 5L Rice Cooker
products.best_for: Larger households or regular batch cooking
products.key_spec: 5L capacity (up to seven people), fuzzy logic, Quick Rice and Delayed Start, steam, slow cook, soup, saute, cake and jam modes
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the fuzzy logic chip produced perfectly cooked basmati, jasmine and brown rice, with a generous 5L capacity that comfortably serves up to seven. The Quick Rice and Delayed Start functions help sync it with meal prep and the extra modes gave snappy steamed veg, a tasty stew and hearty tomato soup, though it isn't the speediest cooker on the list.

specs.Extras: Steam, slow cook, soup, saute, cake, jam/sauce

pros: Consistent, perfectly cooked basmati, jasmine and brown rice
Large capacity feeds up to seven
Quick Rice and Delayed Start functions
Much more versatile than a standard rice cooker
cons: Isn't the speediest rice cooker on the list

guide.q: What is fuzzy logic in a rice cooker?
guide.a: A microprocessor that adjusts cooking temperature and time automatically, giving more consistent results across rice types. The Panda Mini, Cosori and Yum Asia Bamboo here all use it. Expert Reviews notes cooking times vary on such models for that reason, and long times aren't necessarily a disadvantage, since some of the slowest cookers produced the best rice.

guide.q: Do I need a rice cooker if I have a saucepan?
guide.a: Expert Reviews' view is that a good cooker produces consistently high-quality rice even skilled pan cooks can't match, lets you leave it unattended, and keeps it warm for later. Once tried, they say it's hard to go back to saucepan rice, although it's most worthwhile if you eat rice regularly.

Expert Reviews' tested cookers start just over £20 and reach £330, with mid-range models around £100. A cheaper cooker like the Russell Hobbs handles standard white rice well, while higher-priced models use fuzzy logic or induction for more consistent results across rice types.

guide.q: Rice cooker, multi-cooker or pressure cooker?
guide.a: A dedicated rice cooker is simplest. A multi-cooker like the Lakeland Mini or Cosori adds slow cooking, soups and cakes. A pressure cooker such as the Instant Pot Duo Evo Plus here also cooks rice well, in about 22 minutes for three people, and adds fast cooking of tough cuts, making it good value if you'd otherwise buy both.
